name: window.find
description: Find the first top-level window whose title matches `pattern` according to `match` (default `substring`, case-insensitive). Returns `ERR not_found` if no window matches.

pattern.description: Pattern to match against window titles. Interpretation depends on `match`.

match.description: Pattern semantics. `substring` (default, case-insensitive) preserves V2.0 behaviour. `prefix` matches V1 WINFIND parity (case-insensitive prefix). `exact` is case-insensitive equality. `glob` is shell-style with `*` and `?` (case-insensitive, via PathMatchSpecW). `regex` is ECMAScript regex; case-sensitivity is controlled by inline flags (e.g. `(?i)`).

x-implementations.name: enum_windows
x-implementations.description: Win32 `EnumWindows` walk; first window whose `GetWindowTextW` (or A) result satisfies the per-`match` comparator is returned. Walk halts on first match. Comparators: `substring` / `prefix` / `exact` use `_wcsicmp` / `_wcsnicmp` for case-insensitive compare; `glob` uses `PathMatchSpecW`; `regex` uses `std::regex` ECMAScript flavour.

windows-modern.description: EnumWindows + GetWindowTextW + per-mode comparator. Returns the first visible top-level window whose title matches. Hidden windows are not searched (no `--all` flag here; use window.list for that). The 5 match modes: `substring` (default, case-insensitive `_wcsstr`-equivalent — V2.0 behaviour), `prefix` (case-insensitive `_wcsnicmp` — V1 WINFIND parity per issue #75), `exact` (case-insensitive `_wcsicmp`), `glob` (`PathMatchSpecW`), `regex` (`std::regex` ECMAScript).

windows-classic.description: EnumWindows + GetWindowTextW (NT 5+) or GetWindowTextA (NT 4 / 9x, transcoded to UTF-8) + per-mode comparator. Same first-match semantics as modern. `glob` uses PathMatchSpecW (NT 5+) or PathMatchSpecA on NT 4; `regex` requires the agent's bundled regex implementation (no Win32 regex API on classic). All 5 modes available across the family.
